η.def: a primary particle of distinction between two connected terms; disjunctive, or; comparative, than. KJV: and, but (either), (n-)either, except it be, (n-)or (else), rather, save, than, that, what, yea.
an adverb of confirmation; perhaps intensive of ἤ (G2228); used only (in the New Testament) before μέν (G3303); assuredly. KJV: surely.

ηγεμονευω.def: from ἡγεμών (G2232); to act as ruler. KJV: be governor.

ηγεμονια.def: from ἡγεμών (G2232); government, i.e. (in time) official term. KJV: reign.

ηγεμων.def: from ἡγέομαι (G2233); a leader, i.e. chief person (or figuratively, place) of a province. KJV: governor, prince, ruler.

ηγεομαι.def: middle voice of a (presumed) strengthened form of ἄγω (G71); to lead, i.e. command (with official authority); figuratively, to deem, i.e. consider. KJV: account, (be) chief, count, esteem, governor, judge, have the rule over, suppose, think.

ηδεωσ.def: adverb from a derivative of the base of ἡδονή (G2237); sweetly, i.e. (figuratively) with pleasure. KJV: gladly.

ηδη.def: apparently from ἤ (G2228) (or possibly ἦ (G2229)) and δή (G1211); even now. KJV: already, (even) now (already), by this time.

ηδιστα.def: neuter plural of the superlative of the same as ἡδέως (G2234); with great pleasure. KJV: most (very) gladly.

ηδονη.def: from ἁνδάνω (to please); sensual delight; by implication, desire. KJV: lust, pleasure.

ηδυοσμον.def: neuter of the compound of the same as ἡδέως (G2234) and ὀσμή (G3744); a sweet-scented plant, i.e. mint. KJV: mint.

ηθοσ.def: a strengthened form of ἔθος (G1485); usage, i.e. (plural) moral habits. KJV: manners.

ηκω.def: a primary verb; to arrive, i.e. be present (literally or figuratively). KJV: come.

ηλι.def: of Hebrew origin (H410 with pronominal suffix); my God. KJV: Eli.
of Hebrew origin (H5941); Heli (i.e. Eli), an Israelite. KJV: Heli.

ηλιασ.def: of Hebrew origin (H452); Helias (i.e. Elijah), an Israelite. KJV: Elias.

ηλικια.def: from the same as ἡλίκος (G2245); maturity (in years or size). KJV: age, stature.

ηλικοσ.def: from ἧλιξ (a comrade, i.e. one of the same age); as big as, i.e. (interjectively) how much. KJV: how (what) great.

ηλιοσ.def: from ἕλη (a ray; perhaps akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι (G138)); the sun; by implication, light. KJV: + east, sun.

ηλοσ.def: of uncertain affinity; a stud, i.e. spike. KJV: nail.

ημασ.def: accusative case plural of ἐγώ (G1473); us. KJV: our, us, we.

ημεισ.def: nominative plural of ἐγώ (G1473); we (only used when emphatic). KJV: us, we (ourselves).

ημερα.def: feminine (with ὥρα (G5610) implied) of a derivative of ἧμαι (to sit; akin to the base of ἑδραῖος (G1476)) meaning tame, i.e. gentle; day, i.e. (literally) the time space between dawn and dark, or the whole 24 hours (but several days were usually reckoned by the Jews as inclusive of the parts of both extremes); figuratively, a period (always defined more or less clearly by the context). KJV: age, + alway, (mid-)day (by day, (-ly)), + for ever, judgment, (day) time, while, years.

ημετεροσ.def: from θνητός (G2349); our. KJV: our, your (by a different reading).

ημην.def: a prolonged form of ἦν (G2258); I was. KJV: be, was.

ημιθανησ.def: from a presumed compound of the base of ἥμισυ (G2255) and θνήσκω (G2348); half dead, i.e. entirely exhausted. KJV: half dead.

ημιν.def: dative case plural of ἐγώ (G1473); to (or for, with, by) us. KJV: our, (for) us, we.

ημισυ.def: neuter of a derivative from an inseparable prefix akin to ἅμα (G260) (through the idea of partition involved in connection) and meaning semi-; (as noun) half. KJV: half.

ημιωριον.def: from the base of ἥμισυ (G2255) and ὥρα (G5610); a half-hour. KJV: half an hour.

ημων.def: genitive case plural of ἐγώ (G1473); of (or from) us. KJV: our (company), us, we.

ην.def: imperfect of εἰμί (G1510); I (thou, etc.) was (wast or were). KJV: + agree, be, X have (+ charge of), hold, use, was(-t), were.

ηνικα.def: of uncertain affinity; at which time. KJV: when.

ηπερ.def: from ἤ (G2228) and περ (G4007); than at all (or than perhaps, than indeed). KJV: than.

ηπιοσ.def: probably from ἔπος (G2031); properly, affable, i.e. mild or kind. KJV: gentle.

ηρ.def: of Hebrew origin (H6147); Er, an Israelite. KJV: Er.

ηρεμοσ.def: perhaps by transposition from ἔρημος (G2048) (through the idea of stillness); tranquil. KJV: quiet.

ηρωδησ.def: compound of ἥρως (a "hero") and εἶδος (G1491); heroic; Herod, the name of four Jewish kings. KJV: Herod.

ηρωδιανοι.def: plural of a derivative of Ἡρώδης (G2264); Herodians, i.e. partisans of Herod. KJV: Herodians.

ηρωδιασ.def: from Ἡρώδης (G2264); Herodias, a woman of the Heodian family. KJV: Herodias.

ηρωδιων.def: from Ἡρώδης (G2264); Herodion, a Christian. KJV: Herodion.

ησαιασ.def: of Hebrew origin (H3470); Hesaias (i.e. Jeshajah), an Israelite. KJV: Esaias.

ησαυ.def: of Hebrew origin (H6215); Esau, an Edomite. KJV: Esau.

ησυχαζω.def: from the same as ἡσύχιος (G2272); to keep still (intransitively), i.e. refrain from labor, meddlesomeness or speech. KJV: cease, hold peace, be quiet, rest.

ησυχια.def: feminine of ἡσύχιος (G2272); (as noun) stillness, i.e. desistance from bustle or language. KJV: quietness, silence.

ησυχιοσ.def: a prolonged form of a compound probably of a derivative of the base of ἑδραῖος (G1476) and perhaps ἔχω (G2192); properly, keeping one's seat (sedentary), i.e. (by implication) still (undisturbed, undisturbing). KJV: peaceable, quiet.

ητοι.def: from ἤ (G2228) and τοί (G5104); either indeed. KJV: whether.

ητταω.def: from the same as ἥττον (G2276); to make worse, i.e. vanquish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to rate lower. KJV: be inferior, overcome.

ηττημα.def: from ἡττάω (G2274); a deterioration, i.e. (objectively) failure or (subjectively) loss. KJV: diminishing, fault.

ηττον.def: neuter of comparative of ἧκα (slightly) used for that of κακός (G2556); worse (as noun); by implication, less (as adverb). KJV: less, worse.

ητω.def: third person singular imperative of εἰμί (G1510); let him (or it) be. KJV: let … be.

ηχεω.def: from ἦχος (G2279); to make a loud noise, i.e. reverberate. KJV: roar, sound.

ηχοσ.def: of uncertain affinity; a loud or confused noise ("echo"), i.e. roar; figuratively, a rumor. KJV: fame, sound.
